subject: MSA redline: third-party IP claim response lanes & escalation playbook
messages:
From: Evan Patel <evan.patel@brightline.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightLine Legal <legal@brightline.com>
Date: 2029-05-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MSA - Indemnity redlines and claim response lanes

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the call this morning. Our legal team asked for a written proposal on how Redwood would handle third-party IP claims tied to model outputs — specifically: who responds first (customer vs vendor), notice windows, control of defense, and whether there's an evidence-preservation SLA. We reviewed your last redline; attached is BrightLine's counter (v3) with annotated concerns.

Key asks from BrightLine Legal:
- BrightLine to have right to conduct initial triage and, if necessary, retain outside counsel (we'll share counsel details)
- 30-day notice & cure window before triggering indemnity
- Clarify whether Redwood's indemnity covers claims arising from BrightLine's fine-tuning of models

Can you confirm Redwood's proposed fallback language and an estimated timeline for a final redline? We're targeting signature by end of month.

Thanks,

Evan
Evan Patel
Head of Procurement
BrightLine Systems
[Attachment: BrightLine_MSA_Redline_v3.docx]

Hi Evan — thanks for the summary and the redline.

Quick notes:
- Redwood is comfortable with a notice window but 30 days may constrain our ability to investigate; we typically ask for 14 days to acknowledge and 30 days for cure if remediation is possible. We can propose a two-stage notice: 14-day acknowledgement + 30-day cure.
- For customer fine-tuning: that should be scoped — indemnity for vendor-originated model outputs only; we'll propose language distinguishing customer-supplied fine-tunes.
- We'll loop in Legal (Marissa) and Ops to draft fallback and evidence-preservation SLA.

Kimberly/Marissa — can you review Evan's attached and propose concrete redline on the defend/control paragraph and evidence SLA? Evan: we'll push a redline back by tomorrow EOD.

Best,
Dylan
Director, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Dylan/Evan — draft points below (high level) before Marissa sends a full redline:

Proposed compromise (high level):
1) Notice: BrightLine provides prompt written notice; Redwood will acknowledge within 14 days. If BrightLine elects to retain counsel, Redwood retains right to assume defense provided customer has not breached the agreement. If customer-controlled modifications contributed materially to the claim, Redwood's obligation is limited.
2) Control: Right to defend is Redwood's for claims solely attributable to vendor model design or training data. For mixed-cause claims, vendors and customers will engage in good-faith allocation; defense control will be negotiated with an escalation ladder.
3) Evidence SLA: Redwood will preserve relevant logs/kv-cache snapshots for 90 days on request and commit to a 48-hour initial response to evidence preservation requests; further costs for long-term preservation may be subject to reasonable fees.

Open items for discussion:
- Fine-tuning carveout language (how to define customer modifications)
- Insurance offsets and caps

I'll prepare a tracked redline for the defend/control paragraph and include the 14/30 notice ladder. Marissa will finalize tomorrow AM.

kimberly

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood proposed redline & playbook for IP claims (attached)

Evan — attaching Redwood's proposed tracked redline and a short playbook for operational triage. Summary of what we've proposed (see attached "Redwood_Proposed_Defend_Control_Redline.docx"):

- Notice ladder: BrightLine provides notice; Redwood acknowledges within 14 days and confirms investigation plan within 10 business days. If remediation is feasible, a 30-day cure window applies from confirmation of remediation path.
- Defend/control: Redwood will assume control of defense for claims arising solely from vendor model training/data or Redwood-managed outputs. If customer modifications or deployment choices materially contributed, Redwood's indemnity is proportionally limited. We added an escalation ladder (Customer PO -> Sales lead -> Legal counsel) to decide control in mixed-cause claims.
- Evidence preservation: Redwood will preserve logs, inference traces, and a snapshot of relevant KV cache for 90 days on request; initial preservation acknowledgement within 48 hours. Long-term storage (beyond 90 days) will be handled by mutual agreement and may incur storage costs.
- Fine-tuning carveout: proposed definition: "customer-originated fine-tuning" means any model weights or training artifacts provided or generated solely by the customer post-delivery. Claims linked to those artifacts are excluded from Redwood's indemnity.

Attachments included:
- Redwood_Proposed_Defend_Control_Redline.docx (tracked)
- redline_summary_notes.txt (plain summary of each contested paragraph)

Operational asks for BrightLine before we finalize:
1) Confirm whether BrightLine requires initial triage right or is comfortable with Redwood-led triage with customer notification.
2) Confirm whether BrightLine will accept a 14/30 ladder instead of a flat 30-day pre-trigger.
3) Confirm whether BrightLine wants Redwood to commit to a preservation SLA cost cap (we've suggested reasonable fees if >90 days).

If you approve these high-level items we can turn the tracked redline into a signer-ready document and push the DocuSign URL. Target: finalize redline and issue to procurement for countersign by 2029-05-20.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
[Attachments: Redwood_Proposed_Defend_Control_Redline.docx, redline_summary_notes.txt]
